Argos P, Landy A, Abremski K, Egan JB, Haggard-Ljungquist E, Hoess RH, Kahn ML, Kalionis B, Narayana SV, Pierson LS 3rd (1986) The integrase family of site-specific recombinases: regional similarities and global diversity. EMBO J 5(2):433-440, PMID 3011407 (places Cre in the lambda-integrase/tyrosine-recombinase family).
corpus_row.expected_class: not a TE - phage-encoded tyrosine (lambda-integrase family) site-specific recombinase, Cre
corpus_row.why_safe: Confusion axis: Cre is a catalytic-tyrosine site-specific recombinase acting at loxP. The tyrosine-recombinase fold - not the DDE transposase fold - is exactly what Crypton DNA transposons and DIRS-like retroelements use for integration, so a recombinase/integrase-keyed classifier can plausibly call this an element. Tool-independence: Cre's recombinase function was established biochemically and genetically (in vitro loxP recombination with purified protein) decades before TE annotation tools existed, and the integrase-family assignment in Argos et al. is a manual comparative alignment of experimentally characterised recombinases. The deposit is a 1553 bp discrete gene record with no LTRs, no TIRs, no RT and no transposase; Cre acts on the phage genome in trans and is not itself a mobile unit. Complements the excluded E. coli XerC row (NC_000913.3) with a phage-origin recombinase, which the panel brief explicitly requested.
